title: Gull Rock

pages.text:
The rowboat groaned against the mud like a tired old dog. It was Day Four, and the sun hung low and heavy over Saltmarsh Harbor. Juno sat in the bow, her yellow raincoat buttoned tight against the damp chill. She hugged her knees, watching the water lapping at the hull. It was thin, barely enough to float them, but it was there.

"Steady," Teo said from the stern. He was standing on a wooden cart wheel, his green cap pulled low over his messy black hair. His tool belt clinked with every movement. He looked less like a sailor and more like a mechanic who had taken a wrong turn into the sea. "If you look at the water, you’ll get sick. Look at me. I’m very boring."

"I’m not looking at the water," Juno lied. Her stomach gave a nervous flip. "I’m looking at the gulls. They’re very aggressive today."

Above them, a white shape circled in lazy, predatory loops. *Admiral Squawk*, as Barnacle had dubbed him in the log. He let out a shriek that sounded like a rusty hinge.

"Honestly!" Barnacle’s voice came from inside Juno’s pocket, where he clung to the hem of her raincoat. "That bird has the grace of a dropped spoon. Tell him to go away, Juno. Tell him his feathers are matted."

Juno smiled, the tension in her shoulders easing slightly. "I can’t talk to him, Barnacle. I just have to listen."

The cart wheels squelched in the mud as Teo pulled the boat forward. The transition from land to water was a wet, sucking sound that made Juno’s teeth chitter. She took a deep breath, tasting salt and rust.
pages.image: A small wooden rowboat tilting in shallow water, two children inside, a gull swooping low above them, muddy harbor background, soft watercolor style.

pages.text:
The current was gentle, a slow push against the boat’s side. They had left the muddy shore and entered the narrow channel toward Gull Rock. The air smelled of brine and cold iron.

Teo pushed the oars with careful, rhythmic strokes. His hands were wrapped tightly around the wood, knuckles white. Juno could see the vein in his neck pulsing. He was scared. She had seen it before, the way he hovered at the edge of pools, never quite stepping in.

"You’re doing great," she said softly.

"I’m doing fine," Teo corrected, his voice tight. "I’m just... calculating the buoyancy."

"Barnacle says you’re sweating through your tool belt," Juno said.

"Does he?" Teo didn’t look back. "Well, Barnacle is a crab. He’s wet all the time. He doesn’t understand dry skin."

Juno grinned. She reached into her pocket and felt the small, hard shape of the shell whistle. It was warm, as if it had been sitting in the sun. She hadn’t blown it yet. Not here. The Queen had said to listen. So she closed her eyes and let the sound of the water wash over her.

There was a rhythm to it. *Hush-hush, hush-hush.* Like a heartbeat.

"Juno," Teo said, stopping the oars. He pointed ahead. "There."

Gull Rock rose from the water like a jagged tooth. It was dark and jagged, covered in patches of green algae. Perched on top, a single, rusted bell-buoy sat silent. It looked lonely.

"He looks grumpy," Barnacle muttered. "Probably hasn’t been polished since the last century."

Juno nodded. "He’s waiting for us."
pages.image: A view from inside a rowboat looking toward a dark, rocky outcrop with a rusted bell on top, two children rowing, dramatic sky, whimsical ink and watercolor.

pages.text:
The boat scraped against the rocks with a sharp *screech* that made both kids jump. Juno scrambled up the side of the boat, her boots finding purchase on the wet wood. She leaned out, her yellow raincoat bright against the grey stone.

"Teo, hold the boat!" she called out.

"I am holding it with the force of my will!" Teo shouted back, bracing himself against the oars. "Don’t let go! If you fall in, I will not save you. I will document it."

Juno laughed, a bright, sharp sound. She climbed onto the rock face. The stone was slick with algae, cold and slippery under her boots. She had to be careful. One wrong step and she’d be in the water, and she knew, with a sinking feeling, that Teo was watching her every move.

She reached the top of the rock just as the sun dipped lower. The bell-buoy loomed over her. It was massive, painted a faded red that had chipped away to reveal rust underneath. A thick rope was tied around its neck, frayed and weak.

"Okay," Juno whispered to herself. "Listening."

She closed her eyes. The wind died down. The gulls fell silent. In the quiet, she heard it. A faint, metallic hum. *Ting-ting-ting.*

It wasn’t a sound. It was a feeling. A vibration in the air.

"The compass," Barnacle whispered. "It’s inside. The Queen said the Salt Compass is in the bell. You have to ring it."

Juno opened her eyes. She looked at the heavy, iron bell. It was out of reach, hanging just above her head. She would have to climb the pole.
pages.image: A girl in a yellow raincoat climbing a rocky outcrop toward a large, rusted bell, dramatic lighting, focused on her determined expression, watercolor style.

pages.text:
Juno’s fingers found a crack in the rock. She pulled herself up, inch by inch. The air grew colder. The bell hung above her, swaying gently in the breeze.

"I can see it," she said, her breath fogging in the air. "It’s glowing. Just a little."

A soft, blue light pulsed inside the dark interior of the bell. It was beautiful and terrifying.

"Teo, are you seeing that?" she asked.

"I’m seeing a blue light, yes," Teo’s voice came from below, tinny and distant. "I’m also seeing you about to fall. Please don’t fall."

Juno ignored him. She reached up, her hand closing around the cold iron of the bell’s rim. The metal was freezing, biting into her skin. She pulled herself higher, her boots sliding on the wet stone.

"Honestly," Barnacle complained from her pocket. "You’re shaking. It makes my shell rattle. It’s very undignified."

"Shh," Juno whispered. "I’m almost there."

She swung her leg over the pole and dangled there, her toes just touching the ground below. The bell was right in front of her. She could see the Salt Compass inside, a small, intricate device made of brass and silver, spinning slowly in the air.

It was beautiful. It was also very, very high up.

Juno swallowed hard. She reached for it. Her fingers brushed the cold brass. For a second, she froze. The height. The drop. The water below.

*You are not brave, only loud,* the voice in her head whispered.

*No,* she thought back. *I am listening.*

She grabbed the compass. It was warm, like the shell whistle.
pages.image: A close-up of a girl's hand reaching into a dark, glowing bell, blue light illuminating her face, dramatic tension, watercolor and ink.

pages.text:
Juno’s fingers slipped.

The Salt Compass tumbled from her grasp, spinning wildly in the air. It didn’t fall into the water. It landed with a soft *clink* in a narrow crack in the rock face, just below the bell.

"Oh, no," Juno breathed.

"OH, NO!" Barnacle shouted. "It’s in the crack! The crack is wet! If it gets wet, it rusts! And if it rusts, we are all doomed! Honestly, Juno, this is a disaster!"

Juno looked down. The crack was deep, dark, and out of reach. She dangled from the bell’s rim, her arms trembling. The water below was black and deep.

"I can’t reach it," she said, her voice shaking.

"Let me," Teo said.

Juno looked down. Teo was standing on the rock, his face pale. He was looking up at her, then at the crack, then at the water. His jaw was tight.

"Teo," she said. "You don’t have to—"

"I’m fixing it," he said firmly. He reached into his tool belt and pulled out a small, silver wrench. "I’m going to lever it out. It’s physics. I’m good at physics."

He climbed up, his movements stiff and careful. He didn’t look at the water. He looked at the crack.

Juno watched him, her heart pounding. She realized, with a sudden, sharp clarity, that he was doing it for her. He was scared. He was terrified. And he was still climbing.

She felt a surge of warmth in her chest. A hot, bright determination.

She wasn’t alone.
pages.image: Two children on a rocky outcrop, one hanging from a bell, one climbing up to help, dramatic sky, emotional connection, soft watercolor glow.

summary: Juno and Teo travel to Gull Rock in Grandpa’s rowboat, with Teo overcoming his fear of water to row them safely. Juno climbs the bell-buoy to retrieve the Salt Compass but drops it into a rock crack. Teo, despite his fear, climbs up to help her retrieve it using his tools.
